boards.title: Your First Weekend at Lewis University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe Friday-to-Sunday introduction to ten distinct, named destinations on Lewis University’s Romeoville campus.

cards.entity_name: Brother James Gaffney, FSC Student Center
cards.title: Start at the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Find the campus gathering point
cards.notes: Begin in the central lounge, locate Student Engagement downstairs, and use the open gathering space to plan the rest of your route.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented at the campus hub for dining, organizations, games, and informal meetups.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis describes this 26,000-square-foot student center as containing dining, a café and convenience store, organization offices, gaming, and open gathering space.
cards.source_title: Brother James Gaffney, FSC Student Center
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; building access can vary with the academic calendar and university events.

cards.entity_name: Laverne and Dorothy Brown Dining Hall
cards.title: Pause for a First Meal
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Brown Dining Hall
cards.notes: Check the posted service period, then use a meal-plan swipe or another accepted payment method before settling in for dinner.
cards.short_summary: Make the campus dining hall a practical early stop rather than leaving campus immediately.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis places Brown Dining Hall on the first floor of the Gaffney Student Center, and its Welcome Days information lists meal-plan swipes, Flyer Dollars, cash, and credit as accepted payment.
cards.access_notes: Service times vary; consult the current dining schedule before going. Entry for a meal requires an accepted payment method or meal-plan swipe.

cards.title: Find the Brother Statue
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · A mapped Lasallian landmark
cards.notes: Use campus-map marker 13 to find the statue and bench, pause for a clear landmark photo, then continue across the central campus.
cards.short_summary: Learn one visual reference point while beginning to recognize the university’s Lasallian setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis University’s current Romeoville campus map lists “The Brother” Statue and Bench as dedicated-space marker 13.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow university visitor rules and any temporary area closures.

cards.title: Spot the Campus 737
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Aviation history in view
cards.notes: Locate the aircraft from an authorized campus walkway, frame an exterior photo, and avoid entering instructional or restricted aviation areas.
cards.short_summary: Connect the campus landscape to Lewis University’s longstanding aviation education.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis University’s institutional timeline records that the university accepted a donated Boeing 737 aircraft from United Airlines in 1999.
cards.access_notes: View only from authorized public campus areas; aircraft interiors and aviation work areas are not represented as open to visitors.

cards.title: End Friday on the Green
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Central outdoor reset
cards.notes: Walk to campus-map marker 28, identify nearby buildings in daylight, and save the spot as an easy reference for later events.
cards.short_summary: Close the first afternoon with a simple outdoor orientation stop at a named campus space.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Romeoville campus map identifies University Green as dedicated-space marker 28.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; use during suitable weather and observe temporary event restrictions.

cards.title: Learn the Library Rhythm
cards.subtitle: Saturday or Sunday · Plan around posted hours
cards.notes: Find the circulation and research desks, inspect the study-space options, and note that the published schedule closes on Saturdays.
cards.short_summary: Use the first weekend to learn where research help, archives, and reservable study areas are located.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lewis University Library offers research and circulation desks, study-space reservations, and co-located archives; its posted regular hours close Saturdays and run 2–10 p.m. Sundays.
cards.access_notes: As fetched August 13, summer hours run through August 16 and close weekends; regular hours also close Saturdays but list Sunday from 2–10 p.m. Recheck before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Dawn-to-dusk route
cards.notes: Bring water, walk with someone else, remain on the marked trail, and turn back if lightning, high winds, snow, or ice develops.
cards.short_summary: See native Illinois plants on a campus trail with clearly published use and safety rules.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis says the Burnham Centennial Nature Trail contains native plant and tree species, is open dawn to dusk, and asks users to stay on the trail.
cards.source_title: Sustainability Areas — Burnham Centennial Nature Trail
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk. Stay on the marked trail, do not hike alone, and avoid hazardous weather; bicycles, pets, fires, vehicles, and alcohol are prohibited.

cards.title: Trace the Disc Golf Course
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Recreation beside the trail
cards.notes: Locate the mapped course after the trail walk, bring your own discs unless equipment availability is confirmed, and yield to other users.
cards.short_summary: Add a low-key outdoor activity at a specifically mapped campus recreation feature.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis University’s official campus map lists the Disc Golf Course as sports-and-recreation marker 42, and the sustainability page places a Frisbee golf course along the nature trail.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor course access and equipment availability are not stated on the map; check campus notices and avoid play during unsafe weather.

cards.title: Try the Sand-Volleyball Spot
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Behind Sheil Hall
cards.notes: Walk to The Backyard behind Sheil, inspect the sand-volleyball area, and join play only when a university activity or open-use period permits.
cards.short_summary: Learn the location of a named outdoor recreation and social space before the academic week begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis University’s official map identifies The Backyard as recreation marker 25 with sand volleyball, while Welcome Days places student volleyball and social activities there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area; open-play hours are not published on the map. Follow posted reservations, event controls, and weather guidance.

cards.title: Close at Sancta Alberta Chapel
cards.subtitle: Sunday evening · A school-specific gathering place
cards.notes: Check the current worship listing, arrive quietly if attending, and remember that Lewis explicitly welcomes participants from every faith tradition.
cards.short_summary: Finish the weekend at a documented campus chapel that hosts university community gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis identifies Sancta Alberta Chapel as part of the San Miguel Center for Mission and Ministry, and its 2026 Welcome Days schedule lists a Sunday evening Mass there.
cards.source_title: San Miguel Center for Mission and Ministry
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Ministry schedule before attending; worship participation is optional, and building access outside scheduled activities is not guaranteed.

warnings: Indoor access, dining service, recreation availability, and worship schedules can change with the academic calendar; cards conservatively direct users to check current postings.
Unverified card-level coordinates and Google Maps destination URLs are returned as null.
